title: Review B2 (T-0017), rerun on a correctly based worktree: executor routing, per-executor -m, quota-group cooldowns, run-log fields
spec: Adversarial review of the T-0017 diff (commit a01dc3c on task/T-0017, which sits on goal/T-0005 = B1 executors table + fix round). Your worktree is based on task/T-0017, so Pool.pick_executor, cooldown_executor, codex_available(complexity) and the [[executors]] table in .orchestrator/pool.toml exist; verify that first (grep pick_executor orchestrator/pool.py) before judging. The previous review (T-0026) ran on an origin/main worktree and its findings were artefacts of the missing base; ignore them. Review only the changes in orchestrator/executor.py, orchestrator/spawn.py, orchestrator/bus.py and the new tests in tests/test_orchestrator.py from commit a01dc3c (`git show a01dc3c`). Focus: (1) start() picks by the task's real complexity and passes that executor's model to -m; reply() reuses the recorded executor and never re-picks; (2) usage-limit → cooldown_executor cools the whole quota_group; running/day_tasks increments and decrements balance on every path incl. timeout/exception; (3) log_run entries carry executor and complexity; token key normalized to cache_read_input_tokens without losing the Codex value; (4) legacy pool.codex fields keep status() meaningful or are removed consistently; (5) does new code worsen last-writer-wins clobbering of pool_state.json across concurrent Pool() instances; (6) tests assert behaviour, not implementation. Run `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py` in your worktree and report its result line. Return ONLY the review JSON {"verdict":"approve|request_changes","comments":[{"path":"","line":0,"issue":"","severity":"low|med|high"}]}; under 3,000 chars.
acceptance: reviewer confirms pick_executor exists in its worktree before judging
verdict with line-anchored comments on commit a01dc3c only

comments.issue: start() no longer calls pool.codex_available(), which used to reset pool.codex.day/day_tasks on a new day. Now only status()/codex_available() do that reset, so if start() runs before either on a fresh day, pool.codex.day_tasks keeps incrementing against a stale codex.day and never rolls over in that path. Low impact: real routing decisions use ex.day_tasks (correctly rolled via pick_executor's ex.roll_day()), so this only staleness in the deprecated legacy-mirror field pool.codex.*, not a routing bug.

getattr(pool, 'scores', dict)() silently returns {} today since Pool has no scores attribute; if a future B3 change adds self.scores as a plain dict rather than a zero-arg method, this call breaks (dict object not callable). Not exploitable now, worth a comment for whoever wires up B3.

result.unit_tests: python3 -m unittest tests.test_orchestrator: Ran 33 tests in 7.876s - OK
